tasks.spec:
You are an engineer. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the freytag-forge repository (detached at HEAD). Edit files here directly. NEVER git commit, never touch any other checkout, never run `uv`, NEVER call a model (not `claude`, not `codex`), NEVER use the network, never run `python -m bench run`, never write factory/state/. FIRST run: [ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv . Environment for every command: `export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp`. Ruff (python files only): `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check <files>` / `.venv/bin/python -m ruff format <files>` (line length 120, Python 3.12). Never pass --cov to pytest. Run tests as `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 <files>`. Tests must be hermetic (no network, no real model). Shared code must stay story-agnostic (no story, scene or character names in production code; tests may use the repository's real story package and must also cover a synthetic package). ARCHITECTURE RULE (AGENTS.md, firm): world-model logic, meaning anything that reads or changes only world state, is a `World` method in packages/worldkeeper with its tests in packages/worldkeeper/tests; `storygame` only adapts and calls it. If an OLD test pins behaviour this change deliberately changes, update it and say so in NOTES.txt. Write NOTES.txt (worktree root, never committed) listing every ambiguity and your choice. Read first: AGENTS.md, docs/contributor-guide.md, docs/world-model-grounding.md. BACKGROUND. Scenes can now be entered without playing the preceding scenes (hosted `start_scene`, see storygame/runtime/entry_seed.py). Measured: `bare` entry (scene entry fact and placements only) leaves about 110 story facts unset and every earned item hidden at scene 3B; `thorough` entry (a persona that earns everything optional) is path-dependent and also not a state a real player has. The fix is a canonical, versioned entry state per scene: the world after a deterministic player earns only what the route requires. 

You may edit or create ONLY: storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py (new), tests/test_entry_snapshots.py (new), tests/shard_durations.json, docs/world-model-grounding/verification.md, data/stories/continuity-initiative/entry/*.json (generated; one file per scene), and, only if the story loader or its fingerprint or an authoring check must be told to ignore the new directory, the smallest possible change to storygame/story_package/loader.py (say so in NOTES.txt).

ALREADY BUILT (round 23a, in this tree): `World.export_state()`, `World.import_state(state)`, `World.entry_problems(protagonist_id, location_id)` and `worldkeeper.diff_states` in packages/worldkeeper; the `canonical` persona and `advance_state_to_scene(package, state, scene_id, persona=...)` and `canonical_path_report(package)` in storygame/runtime/entry_seed.py (every hop of the real story is an earned transition; the whole path runs in about 2 seconds). Read them and tests/test_canonical_entry_path.py first. Also read storygame/runtime/state.py (`RuntimeState`, `bootstrap`), storygame/runtime/persistence.py, storygame/story_package/dependencies.py (`producers`, `consumers`) and storygame/story_package/loader.py (`_story_package_fingerprint`).

TASK. Build storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py: configuration management of the canonical entry state of every scene. The committed snapshot files are the golden record; code regenerates them and fails when they drift.
1. SNAPSHOT FILE `<story_root>/entry/<SCENE_ID>.json`, deterministic (sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline): {"schema": 1, "story_id", "scene_id", "source_fingerprint", "path": {"persona": "canonical", "turns": n, "storylets_delivered": [...]}, "world": World.export_state(), "story_facts": [sorted {predicate, subject, object, value} for every asserted NON-wk fact], "runtime": the RuntimeState scalar fields needed to resume at the scene entry (current_scene_id, phase, turn_index, scene_entered_at_turn, active_event_ids and fired_event_ids as sorted lists, delivered_cue_ids, cue_stages, staged_* fields, story_complete)}. `source_fingerprint` is a sha256 over the story package's source files EXCLUDING the `entry/` directory itself (reuse the loader's fingerprint approach, but exclude `entry/` so writing snapshots never changes the fingerprint they record). Entry for the FIRST scene is the bootstrap state; every other scene is the state after the canonical path reaches it, exactly at the moment of scene entry. Assert in code (not just in tests) that at a scene entry the fields you do not store (turn_records, pending_break, pending_snapshot, pending_proposal, pending_capture, last_turn_delivery) are at their defaults, and fail loudly if not. If the real model does not satisfy that, say so in NOTES.txt and store what is needed.
2. API: `build_entry_snapshot(package, story_root, scene_id) -> dict`; `write_entry_snapshots(story_root) -> list[Path]`; `load_entry_snapshot(story_root, scene_id) -> dict`; `state_from_snapshot(package, snapshot) -> RuntimeState` which rebuilds the state through `World.import_state` for the world part and the stored story facts and runtime scalars for the rest, then runs `World.entry_problems` for the scene's protagonist and location and raises `EntrySnapshotError` (a ValueError subclass) with the problems when any, and also raises it when `story_id`, `scene_id` or `source_fingerprint` do not match the loaded package. `check_entry_snapshots(story_root) -> list[str]`: plain-words problems, empty when sound: a missing file; a stale fingerprint; DRIFT, meaning the regenerated snapshot differs from the committed one, with a readable summary built from `worldkeeper.diff_states` for the world part and added/removed story facts (cap the message at 40 lines per scene and say how many were cut); entry invariant problems; and the carry-in report's gate problems (below).
3. CARRY-IN REPORT `carry_in_report(package, snapshots) -> list[dict]`: for every scene S and every fact F that has a consumer whose `scene_id` is S (use `consumers`) and whose producers (use `producers`) all belong to EARLIER scenes or are claims not tied to S, one row {scene_id, fact_id, consumer_kind, consumer_id, supplied (F is true in S's entry snapshot), producer_scenes}. A row with `consumer_kind == "gate"` and `supplied == False` is a gate problem reported by `check_entry_snapshots`; wording consumers are listed but are not problems. Be careful about false positives: a fact the scene can produce itself is not carry-in. Whatever the real story gives, do not weaken the rule to make it pass: write the real list of unsupplied gate rows into NOTES.txt and make `check_entry_snapshots` report them (the test asserts the report SHAPE and that a deliberately removed fact in a tampered copy is detected, not that the real list is empty; I will read the real result).
4. CLI: `python -m storygame.runtime.entry_snapshots check [--story-root PATH]` (exit 1 with the problems printed) and `... write [--story-root PATH]`. The default story root is the repository's default story (find how storygame/web_demo.py's `_default_package_root` resolves it, reuse it, do not hardcode a story name).
5. GENERATE and include the real snapshot files for the default story (`entry/1A.json` ... `entry/3C.json`). If the loader, the story package fingerprint cache, an authoring-quality test or tests/test_markdown_story_package.py reject or notice the new directory, make the smallest fix and prove with a test that the package loads identically with and without `entry/` (same fingerprint behaviour for the loader's cache is NOT required if the directory has to be inside the root, but the loaded package must be identical).
6. DOCS: add ONE short bullet to docs/world-model-grounding/verification.md: entry states are golden files; a story change that moves one is reviewed by running the `write` command and reading the diff of `entry/*.json`, committed with the story change. Keep the doc short.

TESTS (tests/test_entry_snapshots.py, hermetic, whole file under 60 s; copy the real story root into tmp_path for any test that edits files): (a) committed snapshots pass `check_entry_snapshots` apart from the carry-in gate rows you record in NOTES.txt (assert on the other problem classes being empty); (b) regenerating twice gives byte-identical files; (c) `state_from_snapshot` for every scene returns a state whose facts and world export equal the canonical path's own state at that scene, and for which `World.entry_problems` is empty; (d) tampering with one committed world fact in a tmp copy is reported as DRIFT with the entity id in the message; removing a story fact is reported; (e) editing a story source file in a tmp copy makes every snapshot stale and `state_from_snapshot` raises EntrySnapshotError; (f) a snapshot that violates an invariant (for example hide a held item in a tmp copy) is refused by `state_from_snapshot`; (g) `carry_in_report` rows have the documented keys, and a synthetic package from the repository's existing test fixtures (find how tests build a small story package) gives a sensible report with a fact produced in one scene and gated in the next; (h) the CLI `check` exits 0/1 accordingly (call `main(argv)`). Add the test file to tests/shard_durations.json with `.venv/bin/python scripts/regen_shard_durations.py --missing-only` (never `uv`; by hand with a measured duration rounded up if that needs network). Run tests/test_entry_snapshots.py, tests/test_canonical_entry_path.py, tests/test_start_scene_session.py, tests/test_world_model.py, packages/worldkeeper/tests, and every test file that loads the story package fixtures (`ls tests | grep -i 'package\|loader'`) to show nothing broke.
tasks.check:
set -eo pipefail
WORK=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/factory-23
mkdir -p "$WORK/out"
export PYTHONPATH=$PWD:$PWD/packages/worldkeeper/src TMPDIR=/tmp
[ -e .venv ] || ln -s /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv .venv
git add -A -- storygame bench tests packages docs data
bad=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep -vE '^(storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots\.py|tests/test_entry_snapshots\.py|tests/shard_durations\.json|docs/world-model-grounding/verification\.md|data/stories/continuity-initiative/entry/[0-9][A-Z]\.json|storygame/story_package/loader\.py)$' || true)
[ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "files outside ownership staged: $bad"; exit 1; }
start=$(date +%s)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n 8 tests/test_entry_snapshots.py tests/test_canonical_entry_path.py tests/test_start_scene_session.py tests/test_world_model.py packages/worldkeeper/tests $(ls tests/test_*package*.py tests/test_*loader*.py 2>/dev/null)
for S in 1A 1B 1C 2A 2B 2C 3A 3B 3C; do [ -s data/stories/continuity-initiative/entry/$S.json ] || { echo "missing entry/$S.json"; exit 1; }; done
.venv/bin/python -m storygame.runtime.entry_snapshots write >/dev/null
git diff --quiet -- data/stories/continuity-initiative/entry || { echo "committed snapshots differ from regenerated ones"; git diff --stat -- data/stories/continuity-initiative/entry; exit 1; }
grep -q 'class EntrySnapshotError' storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py || { echo 'EntrySnapshotError missing'; exit 1; }
grep -q 'carry_in_report' storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py || { echo 'carry_in_report missing'; exit 1; }
if grep -nE "'(1A|1B|1C|2A|2B|2C|3A|3B|3C)'|\"(1A|1B|1C|2A|2B|2C|3A|3B|3C)\"|continuity" storygame/runtime/entry_snapshots.py; then echo 'story names in production code'; exit 1; fi
took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))
echo "checks took $took s (budget 420 s)"
[ "$took" -le 420 ] || { echo "over the 420 s budget"; exit 1; }
PYFILES=$(git diff --cached --name-only | grep '\.py$' || true)
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff check $PYFILES
[ -z "$PYFILES" ] || .venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check $PYFILES
git diff --cached > "$WORK/out/entry-snapshots.patch"
test -s "$WORK/out/entry-snapshots.patch"
tasks.verified: Golden canonical entry snapshots exist for every scene, regenerate byte-identically, load into a valid state, and drift or stale source is caught.
